To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Long-term plasticity of intrinsic neuronal excitability occurs at pre- and postsynaptic sites and can be induced in parallel with long-term synaptic plasticity by STDP protocols.
STDP protocols induce long-lasting changes in the excitability of neurons that are mediated by pre- and post-synaptic mechanisms.
Long-lasting plasticity in intrinsic excitability is induced at both pre- and postsynaptic sites in parallel to long-term plasticity in synaptic transmission.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms underlying the formation of memory traces in the nervous system and the role of the intrinsic neuronal excitabilty in the process of memory storage.
the question how the brain stores information and what the cellular mechanisms underlying information storage are.
the mechanisms underlying learning and memory, and the role of synaptic and intrinsic plasticity in these mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the plasticity of intrinsic neuronal excitability is a general feature of long-term synaptic plasticity.
the induction of long-lasting changes in intrinsic neuronal excitability can be considered as a general phenomenon occurring in parallel with the synaptic plasticity induced by STDP protocols.
STDP is not just a mechanism for synaptic modification, but it is also a potent trigger of intrinsic excitability modifications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

STDP can induce plasticity of intrinsic excitability at both the pre- and post-synaptic sites and that the resulting changes can be spatially extensive and can have important functional consequences for neuronal processing.

STDP is a powerful protocol to induce long-term plasticity at both pre- and postsynaptic sites and that the induced changes in intrinsic excitability may have an important role in the functional integration of the induced synaptic modifications.

STDP protocols are able to induce persistent changes in neuronal excitability at both pre- and post-synaptic sites and that these changes are functionally coupled to the long-term plasticity induced at synapses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the plasticity of intrinsic excitability is a general feature of STDP and it can be observed in both pre- and postsynaptic cells.
STDP protocols induce long-lasting changes in the neuronal intrinsic excitability that may be as important for the information storage as the synaptic plasticity.
the intrinsic excitability is a crucial factor that determines the expression and spatial extent of long-term synaptic plasticity.
